Description: Stable, human-readable primary key for one row in p6_code_crosswalk.csv. Format P6-CODE-NNN with zero-padded three-digit ordinals assigned by sorting scripts/p6/*.py then *.sh alphabetically at inventory time (e.g. P6-CODE-001 = break_glass.py). Uniquely identifies a Code.zip member for citation, audit, and ResearchBox preview. Not a participant ID, Prolific ID, seed, BPB scalar, or AsPredicted number. Scope is this ResearchBox #8918 deposit only; do not reuse IDs across P1.1–P5 boxes.

Path of the inventoried file relative to the git repository root of github.com/pageman/nanochat-filipino (forward-slash POSIX form). Always begins with scripts/p6/. Example: scripts/p6/gate_x_unblind.py. Locates the same bytes in a clone or GitHub browse URL. Not a Runpod absolute path (/root/...), not a Hugging Face weight path, and not a Data-chip CSV path.

Basename only: last path component of relative_path, with extension, no directory prefix. Example: gate_u_seal.py. Matches the leaf name used inside Code.zip under scripts_p6/. Useful for quick visual matching when dragging files. Does not encode gate letter, seed, BPB, or SHA.

File extension including the leading dot. Allowed values in this inventory: .py (Python 3 gate/evaluator/helpers) or .sh (bash launchers sourced under scripts/p6/env*.sh). No .md, .json, .csv, .pt, .pkl, or lockbox plaintext appear in Code.zip. If extension is absent or other, the packer would have flagged a non-code Code.zip member.

Integer on-disk size in bytes of the regular file at inventory generation time (UTC of pack_researchbox_bingo.py run), from Python Path.stat().st_size. Useful to spot truncated uploads or accidental empty stubs. Not token count, not parameter count, not UTF-8 character count, and not the size of the wrapping .zip chip. Re-stat after edits; a changed byte length implies a new sha2_256.

Cryptographic content digest of the exact file bytes, computed as SHA-256 over the full binary/text contents, then prefixed with the literal token sha2-256: (e.g. sha2-256:ab2e1b5e…). Purpose: prove the Code.zip member matches the audited script without redistributing secrets. CRITICAL: this is a FILE hash, not a human/participant/Prolific ID; ResearchBox false-positive ID scanners should be ignored. Not a model checkpoint hash, not AsPredicted PDF SHA, not tokenizer SHA (those live in p6_hashes.csv). Changing even one character changes this value.

Coarse implementation language label used for ResearchBox code search/preview. python = .py files intended for python3 under the pinned nanochat checkout. bash = .sh launchers. Does not imply a ResearchBox-executable runner; reviewers execute offline with scripts/p6/env.sh or env.cuda.sh. Not the training corpus language (Tagalog/English).

Functional family tag grouping scripts by operational role in the P6-M gate spine. Typical values include: gate0, gateA–gateW / gateX / gateP0T / gateQ / gateR / gateS / gateT / gateU / gateV (gate-specific), lib (shared helpers), env (environment), train (parent/child trainers), evaluator (official BPB), seal, prefile (topology schedule builders), deposit (ResearchBox packer), release, ops (tier-2 sync), incident (break-glass / technical accept), test (dummy lockbox harnesses only), paper, other. Tags aid navigation; they do not authorize skipping a gate or amending filed science.

Which filed P6-M gate(s) or stage the file serves, as a short string (e.g. 0, A, H–W, R,S,T, P0-T, U, V, X, W, any, prefile). Multi-gate files may list ranges or comma-separated labels. Maps Code.zip members onto the SHA-bound gate plan (P6-M-GATE-PLAN-FILED.md). Not a pass/fail receipt; receipts are JSON under Other. Parent seed is always 4 when a seed is implied; this study is not a multi-seed panel.

One-line operational description of what the script does in the study workflow (authorize, preflight, train, seal, unblind, pack deposit, refuse unsafe paths, etc.). Descriptive metadata only: it is NOT a confirmatory BPB value, NOT a ΔTL/ΔEN classification, NOT a Policy A test scalar, and NOT a substitute for reading the script or the gate receipt. Dummy harness purposes (Gate 0) are synthetic lockbox tests only.

First leading comment or module docstring line extracted from the file at inventory time (truncated to ~180 characters), if present—e.g. #!/usr/bin/env python3 or a one-line """...""". Aids quick human recognition; may be empty or generic. Not authoritative over the file body or sha2_256. Not a Dear Reader blurb and not paper prose.
